claims.statement: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences published a press release dated 9 October 2024 announcing the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024.

time.note: Date of the Academy's press release; the award ceremony is a separate, later event not recorded here.

claims.qualification: Publication of the announcement only. The release is served on nobelprize.org; the record does not separate the Academy's and the Nobel Foundation's roles in hosting it.

evidence.passage: The release is dated 9 October 2024 and opens with the Academy's statement that it has decided to award the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024.

claims.subject: aib-royal-swedish-academy-of-sciences
claims.statement: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced on 9 October 2024 that it had decided to award one half of the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024 to David Baker “for computational protein design”.

time.note: Date of the Academy's press release; the award ceremony is a separate, later event not recorded here.

claims.qualification: The awarding body's own announcement of its decision; the citation is the Academy's wording. It is not a Selekoa assessment of the work, and it does not attribute the work to Baker alone.

evidence.passage: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences has decided to award the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024 with one half to David Baker University of Washington, Seattle, WA, USA Howard Hughes Medical Institute, USA “for computational protein design”

openQuestions.question: The Nobel release calls Jumper 'Senior Research Scientist at Google DeepMind'; Google DeepMind's post of the same day (dataset atlas-jumper-gdm) calls him 'Director'. Keep both?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep both as separately sourced snapshots; do not reconcile them into one title.

openQuestions.question: Authorship records for ESM-2, ESM3, Evo and AlphaMissense rest on PubMed records (secondary bibliographic metadata) because the Science articles could not be retrieved. Acceptable for admission?
